simple.meaning: חָלַשׁ (châlash) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to prostrate ; by implication, to overthrow , decay.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Exodus, Job, Isaiah, beginning at Exodus 17:13. The surrounding contexts include family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָלַשׁ (H2522) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: חָלַשׁ (châlash) / H2522 is traced through Exodus 17:13, Job 14:10, Isaiah 14:12 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to prostrate ; by implication, to overthrow , decay
definitions.full: H2522. chalash [ חָלַשׁ ] verb 1. be weak, prostrate . 2 (si vera lectio) weaken, disable, prostrate (Aramaic חֲלַשׁ be weak ; , חַלָּשׁ weak , as in Hebrew; Arabic poor (Frey)) — Qal Imperfect וַיַּחֲלשׁ Exod 17:13 , וַיֶּחֱלָ֑שׁ Job 14:10 ; Participle חוֺלֵשׁ Isa 14:12 ; 1 ויח ימות ׳וגבר Job 14:10 but man dieth and is prostrate. 2 disable, prostrate , followed by accusative of person Exod 17:13 (E; point as Hiph`il ?); followed by עַל person (strangely) Isa 14:12 .

occurrences.englishText: Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
But man dies, and is laid low.
How you have fallen from heaven, shining one, son of the dawn! How you are cut down to the ground, who laid the nations low!
